brownian-motion.title: Brownian Motion
brownian-motion.content:
Brownian Motion
Brownian motion is the continuous-time limit of a random walk.
\mathrm{d}X_t = \sqrt{2D}\,\mathrm{d}W_t
where D is the diffusion coefficient and W_t is a Wiener process.
This note connects directly to the interactive Brownian lab in the Astro site and is a good example of the cross-linked research notebook model.

markov-chains.title: Markov Chains
markov-chains.content:
Markov Chains
A Markov chain is a stochastic process where the next state depends only on the current state, not on the full history.
P(X_{n+1}=j \mid X_n=i, X_{n-1}, \ldots) = P_{ij}
This is the defining memoryless property.
Example
For a simple two-state system, the transition matrix can be written as
P = \begin{pmatrix}
1-\alpha & \alpha \\
\beta & 1-\beta
\end{pmatrix}
with transition probabilities between states.

Molecular Simulation
Molecular simulation methods estimate equilibrium or dynamic properties by evolving particle systems numerically.
Typical goals include:

estimating the radial distribution function
sampling configurational states
studying transport and diffusion
validating theoretical models

random-walk.title: Random Walk
random-walk.content:
Random Walk
A random walk is one of the simplest models of diffusion and stochastic motion.
S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k
where X_k are independent increments.
This note serves as a simple example of a browser-based simulation page in the labs section and a conceptual note in the Quartz garden.

statistical-mechanics.title: Statistical Mechanics
statistical-mechanics.content:
Statistical Mechanics
Statistical mechanics studies how microscopic rules generate macroscopic behavior.
A common example is the canonical ensemble, where the probability of a configuration x is
P(x) \propto e^{-\beta E(x)}.
This idea underlies Metropolis sampling, importance sampling, and many simulation workflows.

physics/ensemble-methods.title: Ensemble Methods
physics/ensemble-methods.content:
Ensemble Methods
Ensemble methods are central to sampling and estimating thermodynamic quantities.
Key examples include:

canonical ensemble
microcanonical ensemble
grand canonical ensemble
importance sampling

These ideas are closely tied to Markov Chains and Statistical Mechanics.

physics/non-equilibrium-systems.title: Non-equilibrium Systems
physics/non-equilibrium-systems.content:
Non-equilibrium Systems
A non-equilibrium system is driven by gradients, forcing, or external baths, so it does not stay at equilibrium.
Examples include:

diffusion
drift-dominated flows
reaction-diffusion systems
driven lattice models

This note connects to Random Walk, Brownian Motion, and Markov Chains.

physics/phase-transitions.title: Phase Transitions
physics/phase-transitions.content:
Phase Transitions
Phase transitions occur when a system changes collective behavior as parameters vary.
Examples include:

liquid-gas transitions
magnetic ordering
percolation
structural changes in simulation models

This topic connects to Statistical Mechanics and to lattice simulations described in the lab section.
